study_focus: Properties of real and complex number systems
Basic properties of natural numbers and divisibility
The Euclidean Algorithm and mathematical induction
domain_guidance.summary: Focuses primarily on the core properties of real and complex numbers, proportional relationships, dimensional analysis, divisibility rules, mathematical induction, the Euclidean Algorithm, and the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic for candidates.

study_focus: Real and complex numbers as fields
General properties of functions and linear algebra
domain_guidance.summary: Covers notable algebraic structures, fields and rings, advanced polynomial equations, the Rational Root Theorem, general properties of functions, linear algebra principles, vectors, and matrices for prospective teachers preparing for certification.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at your designated computer-based testing center on time. Manage your 150 minutes across the 52 questions carefully, keeping in mind that calculators are strictly not allowed.

faq.answer_text: The official computer-based examination contains a total of 52 questions, which are presented to candidates in both multiple-choice and constructed-response formats during the testing period.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The required passing score for this certification test is established exactly at 220, which candidates must achieve on the official scale to successfully pass the subtest.
This computer-based examination has a total duration of 150 minutes, providing candidates with adequate time to complete all required questions within the designated testing session.
The exam price is set at $99 per subtest, and candidates pursuing a Single Subject credential take three subtests for a combined total cost of $297.
faq.question_title: How much does the exam cost?

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the CSET Mathematics Subtest I exam, covering number and quantity as well as algebra concepts for prospective educators seeking certification.

methodology.summary: This detailed overview was developed using official CSET exam guides and certification documentation to outline domain structures and relevant testing parameters clearly.

editorial.overview: The CSET Mathematics Subtest I computer-based examination evaluates prospective educators on fundamental mathematical subjects including number and quantity, alongside advanced algebra concepts. Certified by CSET, this subtest forms a notable part of the official credentialing process for aspiring mathematics educators seeking professional licensure across authorized testing centers during their certification journey.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Carefully review the complex number and quantity systems alongside abstract algebraic structures and polynomial equations before your test session. Practice solving challenging mathematical problems using mathematical induction, the Euclidean Algorithm, and various functions without relying on a calculator to ensure full readiness for all 52 questions.
editorial.who_should_take: Candidates who are actively pursuing a Single Subject Teaching Credential in mathematics take this computer-based test to comprehensively demonstrate their relevant knowledge in algebra and number theory.

exam_name: CSET Mathematics Subtest I (Algebra & Number Theory)
exam_price_notes: $99 per subtest. CSET Math requires Subtests I, II, and III for Single Subject credential ($297 total). 45-day wait between retakes.
